Without more information, you're about to make a decision based on your daughter's feelings rather than what's actually going on in the classroom.

First, talk to your daughter about specific incidents: What did the teacher say? What happened? What did she do? Then talk to the teacher yourself. Most teachers welcome parent communication and may not be aware of how their classroom management is affecting students. You might discover the teacher isn't actually being mean — or you might find out something serious is happening. Either way, you'll have more information than you do right now.

If after talking to both parties you still believe the teacher is genuinely inappropriate, then you can escalate to the principal. But going straight there without understanding the full picture will likely get you nowhere and may damage your relationship with the teacher and school. Your daughter needs you to be her advocate, not just to act on her feelings.
